articles.title: Brighter Than The Sun: How Lionsgate Marketing & PR Turned B.O. Around For 'Sunrise On The Reaping'
articles.summary: In the wake of Lionsgate's last Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes hitting a franchise low at the box office, the Santa Monica, CA based studio got very serious — serious about marketing and reaching the younger audience segemts that the conglomerate built their brand upon with franchises such as Twilight and, of […]
articles.content:
In the wake of Lionsgate 's last Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes hitting a franchise low at the box office, the Santa Monica, CA based studio got very serious — serious about marketing and reaching younger audiences that the conglomerate built their brand upon with franchises such as Twilight and, of course, Suzanne Collins' Hunger Games.

Three years ago, it looked like the Hunger Games series petered out with a $44.6M domestic, and $100.8M WW opening and final of $166.3M domestic and $363.9M WW. But this weekend like a death-dying act by Katniss Everdeen herself, Lionsgate completely resuscitated the franchise from its rock bottom as prequel Hunger Games: Sunrise of the Reaping rose like a phoenix, leaving the previous installment's box office ashes in the dust with a great $120M domestic, $225M global opening. Among prequels at the domestic B.O., Sunrise on the Reaping 's was second best after Rogue One: A Star Wars Story 's $155M start. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News 'Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping' Returns Lionsgate Franchise To Fortune With $120M+ U.S. Opening - Box Office Update Books 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping' Album Boasts 29 Songs; Releases Ahead Of Film

That worldwide B.O. on Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes was worse than any installment in another popular YA franchise, the Harry Potter prequel/spinoff series Fantastic Beasts (the lowest being the last film, 2022's The Secrets of Dumbledore with $407.1M). Songbirds & Snakes repped the first time that Collins had written an origins story about one of the core characters, specifically, its villain Coriolanus Snow in a mentorship love story with District 12 tribute Lucy Gray Baird. There was a big bluegrass music element in the film, with Olivia Rodrigo on the soundtrack. Lacking in the movie was an OG cast member from the first four films given that it took place 64 years before the events of the first Hunger Games novel. Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The novel was flat out rejected by fans, some pointing to Covid as an easy reason, others to the fact that it was about the bad guy, with 500K first week copies sold and final reported figure of 2.5M. Complicating business further was the fact that Songbirds & Snakes opened at the box office shortly after the actors strike ended. Even though Lionsgate, as an indie studio, had a SAG-AFTRA waiver for the cast to promote, it was still a challenge to prop a tentpole during such times. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Collins marched on and figured out what her fanbase needed, crafting her next novel, Sunrise on the Reaping about the rise of Katniss and Peeta mentor Haymitch Abernathy (played by Woody Harrelson in the first four films). There was an epilogue in the book, not just with the older Haymitch, but Peeta and Katniss as well. It was the novel that fans wanted and they showed their love by snapping up 4.4 million copies around the globe. It was also a good enough roux for filmmaker Francis Lawrence, director on films 2-5, to work from. In a complete one-up from Songbirds & Snakes, Lionsgate brought back the original 2012 pic's screenwriter, Oscar nominated Billy Ray, to adapt Collins' latest.

In July 2025, Lionsgate saw a changeover in their marketing and publicity with then EVP Strategy and Chief of Staff Amanda Kozlowski, EVP Worldwide Publicity Nasim Cambron and EVP Global Creative Advertising Jack Teed stepping up. Such exec maneuvers ultimately left Lionsgate all the richer with a female tentpole destination in last Christmas' Sydney Sweeney and Amanda Seyfriend thriller The Housemaid ($400.4M, first weekend turnout of 18-34 was 63%) fueled by a dish plate smashing social media meme, and of course, the studio's first billion dollar grossing movie last summer, the Michael Jackson biopic, Michael. Kozlowski was promoted to Worldwide Marketing President in May shortly after Michael 's $218.8M global opening, in addition to Cambron being elevated to EVP, Worldwide Marketing & Publicity and Teed to EVP, Worldwide Marketing & Creative Advertising. Chris Daniel, SVP, Global Creative Marketing and other members of the Lionsgate Marketing team also get shoutouts here for this weekend's B.O. success.

"There is a new generation of marketing brains who understand how people are communicating with one another and how marketing messages can make an impact. The leaders of our marketing group, digital, media, publicity and creative teams are going 14 months strong with The Long Walk, Now You See Me, Now You Dont, Housemaid, Michael , and they're not doing things in traditional ways. They’re creating moments that permeate popular culture and get audiences excited and want to share them with their friends," said Lionsgate Motion Picture Chairman Adam Fogelson today in celebration of Sunrise on the Reaping.

Previously at a Deadline Regal event over the summer, Fogelson told us that, “All of the things when I was growing up in marketing that were sort of held to be certain and true about how you reach an audience, those things, especially for the generations we’re talking about, have changed." Case in point: Don’t overshare too much in a trailer; if you do, “you’re going to get flat-out rejected,” he added at the time. “Some of the movies that are succeeding that are coming from this generation, they’re telling story in a very different way,” said Fogelson.

The overarching strategy for Sunrise on the Reaping was to make the sixth installment of the 14-year old franchise feel like the biggest games yet, not only reigniting the passion of longtime fans with a fave character in Haymitch, but also introducing a new generation to Panem.

A longtime motion picture marketing exec going back to Universal, Fogelson's campaigns were always known for being anchored in character. Sources say Kozlowski has a similar philosophy, but also that the exec knows how to sell story and how to sell to a fanbase. At the center of this Hunger Games promo was Joseph Zada nailing a portrayal of a younger Haymitch.

Kozlowski tells Deadline, "From the beginning, Sunrise on the Reaping had a lot to offer Hunger Games fans — a fan-favorite character whose backstory many had long been asking for, the scale and spectacle of the biggest Games ever and a throughline that connected Haymitch’s tragedy to the rise of the revolution that culminated with Katniss. The marketing team combined those elements with a fan-forward campaign rooted in Gen Z and Gen Alpha online culture, peak Millennial nostalgia, activations that brought the world of Panem into our own and a wealth of unforgettable cast and filmmaker moments. As fans ourselves, it’s been gratifying to see moviegoers responding to the campaign with as much enthusiasm as we have for the world that Suzanne, Francis and Nina (Jacobson) have so lovingly created.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

The drumroll for Sunrise on the Reaping began a year ago when Lionsgate dropped the first teaser to 109 million global views in 24 hours, which became the studio's second-most-watched trailer ever after Michael which they had just debuted a few days prior. At the time that trailer traffic for Sunrise was +48% ahead of Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes , an excellent sign.

From there, Lionsgate created a card stacking (to use a Sunrise word) of high-impact reveals and cultural moments all the way up to release. The studio turned the casting announcements into a pop culture even with 16 individual announcements that generated 541 million views and 35.2 million engagements.

When it came to the late campaign unveiling of the 29-song soundtrack, the studio executed a staggered, artist driven rollout with such performers as Noah Kahan, The Smashing Pumpkins, Ella Langley and Gigi Perez. Altogether this part of the pic's marketing, which sought to expand beyond the franchise's core, yielded 40 million+ social views and 186 playlist placements.

A glittery part of the pic's push was bringing Panem into the real world with immersive activations, fashion and lifestyle partnerships, and cultural integrations. Lionsgate set up Sunrise Gardens installations across 30 countries and six continents including Peru, Sweden, Brazil, South Africa, Denmark, Belgium, Singapore, Finland, London and more, which was picked up across social media.

The marketing also leaned into the pic's themes of Capitol Propaganda with a customized Election Day activation across CNN and Fox News generating 79M+ social impressions and repping 31% of the Sunrise social conversation the following day.

Timed to Paris Fashion Week, there was the Elegance Is Authority exhibition at the Musée Rodin attracted 10,000+ registrations in 24 hours.

Also, there were beauty and fashion partnerships with Stila Cosmetics and Depop. Stila's collaboration reached 1,500+ Ulta stores and generating 50 million+ press and organic social impressions.

In appealing to Gen Z and Gen Alpha, Lionsgate embraced creators, platforms, humor and content creators, inviting them to participate in the franchise rather than simply consume its marketing. Read, the studio teamed with a 16-year-old viral fan editor on the franchise's first official fan-edit trailer, which pulled in 60.3 million+ views on TikTok. A global fan casting contest inspired 7,500+ submissions and 195.6 million+ views on fan-created videos, with participation extending beyond the core fandom to KATSEYE , Zooey Deschanel and Disney's Stitch .

Toward the end, Sunrise on the Reaping 's propaganda built to a crescendo of peak nostalgia by paying homage to the old in the new. Specifically, Lionsgate made a point to rope in OG cast members Harrelson, Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson with bookings on The Tonight Show and Bravo's Watch What Happens Live.

In the end, a great report card of stats for Sunrise 's push, i.e. 1 billion+ owned-social views, 691M TikTok views, and 74 billion+ views of fan-generated content across relevant Hunger Games TikTok hashtags; 1.5 million new followers across the pic's official social channels with a massive turnout by the 18-34 at 72% in PostTrak exits. The movie was the No. 2 pic on TikTok's Trending Chart, behind only Avengers: Doomsday . Conversation volume on X was more than 4x than Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes at the comparable point in its campaign. The digital campaign was overseen by Lionsgate EVP, Head of Worldwide Digital Marketing, Briana McElroy. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

The campaign for Sunrise on the Reaping generated renewed enthusiasm among women 17-34 who gave it a 36% first choice versus 24% for Ballad of Songbirds and Snake. Women under 25 showed up at 38% for Sunrise on the Reaping per PostTrak exits.

Overall, the media and social reach for the Sunrise push clocked 2.7 billion+ paid media impressions with heavy play on the NFL, NBA, World Series, and shows such as Saturday Night Live , The Voice , Abbott Elementary , The Traitors , and the Real Housewives .

In the end, Sunrise on the Reaping pulled in 7.1 million admission this weekend stateside per EntTelligence, +122% from the 3.2M opening weekend admissions of Songbirds & Snakes three years ago.

You could say that the odds were greatly in the favor of Sunrise of the Reaping 's marketing campaign.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Needs to Retcon One of Its Weirdest Android 18 Choices
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation The story of Dragon Ball is known for being goofy and off-beat beyond the battlefield. For all its serious moments, the story features characters with food names, an afterlife where bad guys are tortured by fairies and Mr. Satan changing to Hercule in the English dub and more amongst other numerous funny bits. One weird […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The story of Dragon Ball is known for being goofy and off-beat beyond the battlefield. For all its serious moments, the story features characters with food names, an afterlife where bad guys are tortured by fairies and Mr. Satan changing to Hercule in the English dub and more amongst other numerous funny bits . One weird bit that should've received another edit before making the final cut, however, is Android 17 and 18's name choice.

Android 17 and 18 are introduced as killing machines in Dragon Ball Z . They were kidnapped and created by the Red Ribbon Army's Dr. Gero to kill Goku and take over the world. Their almost emotionless violence and super-powered abilities gave them a robot feel. Once Cell is defeated, the human part of them is restored, but their human names are not. It was revealed later by franchise creator Akira Toriyama that their names are Lapis (17) and Lazuli (18 ), however they were never brought into the manga or anime.

Android 17 becomes a park ranger after the events of the Cell Saga and falls off the radar. Even though this point applies to him too and he deserves to have his name be something other than a number, the plot doesn't awkwardly point it out time after time. Android 18 on the other hand marries Krillin, gives birth to Marron and becomes a member of the Z Fighters. And yet, her name stays simply, "18." Anytime Krillin addresses her it's that same number. An unceremonious way to address one of the anime's fan favorite characters .

Plot-wise it makes sense to change it. The androids went from humans to bio-mechanical beings, so the number applies and fits their evil personas. Once they've transformed back to being normal people, however, a human name makes more sense for a "new-ish" beginning to their lives. The scene from Dragon Ball Super where Future Trunks sees her for the first time since their fight would still have the same terror and humor when he sees her as he associates the name Android 18 with something evil.

Lazuli is much more disarming, and would have changed that interaction overall. Then again, would you expect any less focus toward mid-card characters ? They're regularly forgotten in the series.

The awkwardness is only further focused in on when you remember that the Android twins were featured much more in Dragon Ball Super, especially towards the end. It's one of the flaws of creating such an expansive universe as some characters are bound to be sidelined for a certain amount of time. The only way to get more information on those characters is either to have a whole side arc or series about a particular individual.

In Dragon Ball Super , fans got to see the pure hearts of Android 17 and 18. They battled for their home universe valiantly, and 17 got the wish for winning the Tournament of Power. He could've chosen whatever he wanted, even though it was expected he'd ask for something selflessly. He wished back all the erased universes, and it's an action that a former robot (and someone with "Android" in their name) would never do.

Do you think the Android twins should get their real names brought into the official Dragon Ball canon? Let us know in the comments.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you grew up in the '80s or '90s, think back to Saturday mornings in the early 1990s. Once you were out of bed, you poured yourself some sugary cereal, plopped down in front of the television, and watched what seemed like a never-ending amount of cartoons. Being part of that generation, you got two decades' worth of cartoon fun. There was no shortage of animated action heroes to choose from. One station would be promoting a team of superheroes, some bizarre alien invasion, or a group of unlikely heroes getting ready to save the world.

Here's what's so great about these cartoons. We can think back to the hits, and that's what we have to compare everything to, but there were a whole lot of unique cartoons competing for our attention. So much so that we might've missed a bunch of them. There were shows with silly plots and ideas that somehow worked, and shows that were headed toward having the fan bases and ideas to become something bigger. And with no internet or streaming, you rarely got another chance. As a result, maybe you watched them before school or during Saturday morning cartoons when you were a kid, or maybe you forgot about them entirely.

Get this: three mice battle an evil businessman with motorcycles. Come on, is there any way this cartoon could have been more perfect for a young boy in the early '90s? Biker Mice from Mars was an extremely cheesy cartoon with the kind of storyline that you would expect to see during the era. And the cheese was good. It starred three mice with motorcycles, Throttle, Vinnie, and Modo, who fled their home planet after the Plutarkians, a race of fish-like aliens, devastated their homeworld and turned their attention to Earth. The bad guys included a businessman named Lawrence Limburger, who was out to take over Earth.

What you got was everything you could possibly want from a cartoon made in the early '90s about action and motorcycles: giant bikes, giant villains, and endless explosions. And while all that blowing things up involved plenty of robots and space pirates, Throttle, Vinnie, and Modo all had very different personalities, and that really kept the show interesting. There was Throttle, the cool, arrogant one; Vinnie, the adrenaline addict; and Modo, the one with the sweet robot arm. Essentially, it was a superhero story, just with a lot more Bozo the Clown biker BS and silly sci-fi set design. It's unfortunate that it ended, but at least the guys did get their own reboot. Not enough cartoon stories ever have a handful of motorcycles and fish-faced aliens.

If you were a kid in the early '90s and tuned into Saturday morning cartoons, you were likely to see at least one episode of Bucky O'Hare . He's a green rabbit (who also happens to be a space captain) traveling the galaxy with an adorable crew of misfit warriors. Not so lovable was his chief arch-nemesis (sort of): the Toad Empire, an empire of sticky amphibians hell-bent on world domination. Quirky? Yep. Great? Totally. And just like the comic book it was adapted from, the cartoon series was a little peculiar.

Bucky was joined by Deadeye Duck, Jenny the cat, and Willy DuWitt, a human boy who suddenly became stranded in their world. They fought against the Toad Empire and its increasingly bizarre minions and creations. There was no end of memorable characters and a ton of battles.. It had a memorable theme song, and it just felt like one big Saturday morning affair. Bucky O'Hare only lasted a paltry 13 episodes, which is a shame for a cartoon that had so much potential. Tragic. It was one of my faves for sure. Hunting down the toys was extremely difficult, to boot. Nevertheless, it found a solid following and was one of the more entertaining adventures that history has unfortunately forgotten. Sometimes, even a spacefaring rabbit needs to get a little more time.

There were a whole lot of mutant animal or giant monster cartoons in the '90s. The Bots Master was a bit different. Instead of monsters, we got a teenage boy and his incredible army of robots. Ziv Zulander is a brilliant young robotics engineer who discovers that the company he works for, the Robotic Megafact Corporation, has plans for world domination. With his own army of robots, he sets out to expose the company's schemes. No pressure, Ziv. And I was a big fan of this one. My best friend and I would call each other after each episode aired and talk about it. Good times.

The robots, of course, were a big part of the appeal of the show. Ziv had his small army of metallic friends who helped him battle evil, but there was plenty of sci-fi action and special effects to keep the story moving. It also allowed computer-generated animation to play side by side with standard animation, and it had a distinctive look compared to many other cartoons of its day. Maybe it wasn't the best marketed, but there's something about it that makes a part of me feel all fuzzy inside when I see those sci-fi cartoons from the early '90s that imagine the future as being stuffed to the gills with big corporations and a whole lot of tech. That's the kind of future I wanted to grow up in. And we're almost there. I still have fond memories of The Bots Master and collecting the toys from the show.

With so many superhero cartoons on the air in the 1990s, it's easy to forget that WildC.A.T.s ever existed. Based on the underrated comic book by Jim Lee and Brandon Choi, the series focused on a group of heroes who had to take on an ancient extraterrestrial threat known as the Daemonites. It was the perfect alternative to the X-Men and had its own unique appeal that made it one of my favorite comics to read and collect. I still have all my original issues, and unlike some fans, the '90s are my favorite era of comics.

All of the characters in WildC.A.T.s had very different powers and, well, personalities. Spartan was a highly advanced android, Warblade could turn his entire body into weapons, and Grifter was full of attitude. There were even alien plots, murderers, and everything you would expect from a superhero cartoon on a kids' show in the '90s. Unfortunately, the series was not quite as long-running as it should've been, especially when compared to Batman: The Animated Series or the X-Men cartoons. Regardless, it was quite the feat to get an indie comic from a new comics publisher onto TV and make it part of Saturday morning cartoons. It was ambitious, cool, and as '90s as you can get. Fans of comic books, especially fans of the '90s, need to put this one on their list of must-watch cartoons.

Cadillacs and Dinosaurs is a truly great American cartoon. It had high-tech contraptions, mutants, and big American muscle cars. How ridiculously random is this four-way mashup of a combo? But it's awesome. Based on the comics ( Xenozoic Tales ) of Mark Schultz, the TV series depicts a future Earth where mankind has survived a worldwide ecological catastrophe, dinosaurs are cohabiting again, and a new civilization is being created from nothing alongside these prehistoric giants.

The show followed mechanic Jack Tenrec and scientist Hannah Dundee (who's also an ambassador) as they lived and thrived in this deadly world. Jack was a little bit obsessed with his old-school Cadillac, and you can kind of see why, considering the rest of this future included more heavy-duty equipment and far fewer vintage cars to drive around. The whole thing is unapologetically masculine. I've rewatched this entire series again recently, and it has not aged poorly one bit. It's also still very unique, and I highly recommend you watch it! As a matter of fact, watch everything on this list!

What about you? Did you grow up watching any of these forgotten cartoons, or is there another hidden gem from the '90s that deserves a spot on this list? We'd love to hear which shows you remember, which ones you still love, and which ones you think deserve another look. Share your favorites in the comments below!

The K-pop group Ateez continued its string of chart successes with the No. 1 bow on the Billboard 200 album chart of "Golden Hour: Part 6." It's the third time in 2026 that the group has had an EP debut in the top spot; the last such occasion came in July, when they premiered at No. 1 with (you guessed it) "Golden Hour: Part 5," and they did it with "Part 4" before that in February.

Billboard reported that the tally was almost entirely sales-driven, with individual copies that were sold amounting to 191,000 of the 195,000 total. A big factor in the massive physical sales, as is typical for K-pop, was the availability of substantial variants designed to encourage multiple sales among fans, with different collectible items in each package — 32 such vinyl or CD variations altogether, Billboard said.

articles.title: I’ve Been Worried About 9-1-1’s Buck And Eddie, And The EP Explained Where They Stand After The Latest Midseason Finale
articles.summary: Things have been very intense.
articles.content:
Warning! Spoilers ahead for the Season 10 fall finale of 9-1-1 , “Et Tu?,” which is available to stream with a Hulu subscription .

Buck’s big decision in the Season 9 finale to foster his biological son following the death of his parents has led to some difficulties at the start of Season 10. The toddler, Theo, is a bit rambunctious and doesn’t take well to authority. This has put a strain on Buck’s relationship with Eddie, who knows what it’s like to be a single father. It doesn’t help that after Buck decided to give Theo up , Eddie became his foster dad through emergency placement. This has put even more pressure on them, and EP and showrunner Tim Minear told TV Insider why they went in this direction:

Buck had donated sperm to his friend and his wife, who were having trouble conceiving a few seasons ago, and after helping her deliver, it didn’t really come up again...until last season. Then, after the couple died in a car crash, Buck felt responsible for the kid and took him in. There was some concern for Buck going into Season 10 , and it was obvious this wasn’t going to be easy, especially after seeing Theo’s chaotic energy. So he ultimately believed that Theo would be better with someone else.

Despite the growing tension in the midseason finale, Buck and Eddie had somewhat made up towards the end of the episode. While Buck wasn’t quite ready to see Theo, he understood why Eddie did what he did. It’s hard to tell where things will go for them in the new year, but with Theo staying with Eddie and Buck coming to terms with everything, it should be interesting. On that note, Minear shares that both of them will have some growing to do for multiple reasons:

I have been worried about Buck and Eddie’s relationship since the beginning of the season, when it was clear that Buck fostering Theo would bring some problems. And it didn’t get any easier when Eddie became the foster parent. I’m definitely glad that they’ve crossed a barrier, and they both realize how they acted in this situation might not have been the best. However, I am looking forward to seeing what happens now that they have an understanding with each other and Theo.

articles.title: This Golden Age Flash First Appearance Could Be Worth $234,000, But There's a Catch
articles.summary: Only a handful of Golden Age comics can come close to matching the historical significance of 1940's Flash Comics #1. The issue introduced readers not only the Scarlet Speedster, but the original Golden Age incarnation of Hawkman, and beloved Justice Society of America mainstay Johnny Thunder and his Thunderbolt. Plus, the issue introduces Shiera Sanders, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Only a handful of Golden Age comics can come close to matching the historical significance of 1940's Flash Comics #1. The issue introduced readers not only the Scarlet Speedster , but the original Golden Age incarnation of Hawkman , and beloved Justice Society of America mainstay Johnny Thunder and his Thunderbolt. Plus, the issue introduces Shiera Sanders, the original Hawkgirl — though she doesn't take on her heroic alter-ego until the following year's All-Star Comics #5. This is where DC began to build a universe, debuting heroes who would soon become charter members of the Justice Society of America. Before Flash Comics #1, the heroes of the DC Universe consisted of Superman , Batman , Zatara , and the Crimson Avenger. By the end of 1940, that roll call would expand to include Robin , the Spectre , Hourman, Doctor Fate, and the Green Lantern. The epicenter of that super-hero explosion, which would earn the "Golden Age" its name, began here. It's no wonder, then, that the Overstreet Price Guide lists this as the twelfth most valuable comic of the era — unrestored, of course.

Comic book restoration is a long-standing and controversial collecting practice. For decades, it was acceptable to pay a professional or to attempt at home to improve the condition of a vintage comic book. As comic book grading became common practice, restoration came to be seen as "cheating" the grade, artificially inflating the book's value. As a result, restored books are often worth a mere fraction of the price of an unrestored copy, even when the issue in question is a Golden Age mega-key like Flash Comics #1. The CGC (Certified Guarantee Company) lists less than one hundred copies of Flash Comics #1 on their population report. In an unrestored 8.0 grade, Heritage Auctions quotes a value of $234k . But the copy on auction through Heritage later this week was the recipient of extensive restoration, making it an "apparent" rather than a true 8.0. At the time of writing, this looks to be a $200k difference, as the current price sits just shy of $27k.

While DC's "big three" (Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman) are products of the Golden Age, they transcended the era, evading cancellation at its tail end and evolving to suit a changing medium . If you say "Golden Age" to a DC Comics fan, they'll instead think of the heroes of the Justice Society, rooted in and defined by the era that spawned them. These characters emerged from the culture and the conventions of the 1940s, embodying the courage and determination of an America in the midst of World War II. After their initial retirement at the decade's close, a conscious decision was made by subsequent creators to keep these characters frozen in time. Gardner Fox created "Earth-Two" for them to inhabit, and though time passed there and its heroes aged (Earth-Two's Superman is distinguished by his graying temples, after all), it always felt like the Golden Age never ended. Even Crisis on Infinite Earths did little to change this, collapsing the multiverse but retaining the World War II-era for the heroes of the Justice Society.

Much of this owes to the storytelling, with the origins of Jay Garrick's Flash, Carter Hall's Hawkman, and Johnny Thunder feeling distinctly old-fashioned. As written in Flash Comics #1, college student Jay Garrick is experimenting with "hard water" (water with a high mineral concentration, for those of us who didn't pay attention in science class) when he accidentally gains super-powers from minerals in the water's vapor combining with the chemicals in the cigarette he is smoking. Ret-cons would change this from "hard water" to "heavy water," a key component in atomic bomb research. Taking on the identity of "the Flash," Garrick first dismantles a protection racket operating in his home of New York City, then foils a spy ring that have kidnapped his girlfriend's army major father. Garrick would headline the Flash until its 1949 cancellation, as well as All-Flash Quarterly from 1941 to 1947. He also appeared in Justice Society stories in All-Star Comics beginning in 1941 and lasting until 1951. After All-Star Comics ' cancellation, Garrick would not appear again until Gardner Fox's landmark The Flash #123, when he would team up with his Earth-One successor Barry Allen for the first time.

The Carter Hall iteration of Hawkman drew influence from Universal's The Mummy with its themes of ancient Egyptian reincarnation. Hall was an archaeologist and the reincarnation of Egyptian Prince Khufu, murdered along with his lover Chay-Ara by jealous priest Hath-Set. When Hall touches the ancient Nth metal dagger Khufu used to kill Khufu, he regains his memories of his past life. Creating the costume and Nth metal anti-gravity belt of "Hawkman," Hall rescues Chay-Ara's reincarnation, Shiera Sanders, from Hath-Set's reincarnation, Anton Hastor. This became the basis for a notorious continuity headache after Crisis on Infinite Earths , which had to square the "reincarnated Egyptian prince" Hawkman with the Silver Age "alien policeman" Hawkman introduced by Gardner Fox in 1961's Brave and the Bold #34. As well as joining the Flash in founding the Justice Society, Hawkman served with distinction in Roy Thomas's fan favorite All-Star Squadron , a World War II-set love letter to the Golden Age heroes and villains of DC Comics.

Johnny Thunder is a comparative footnote, but a fondly remembered one among JSA fans. The character is kind of ridiculous, and his origin is laden with poorly-aged Orientalist stereotypes. Johnny is the seventh son of a seventh son, kidnapped by mystics of "Badhnesia" for an occult ritual on his seventh birthday. Instead of bringing power to the Badhnesians, the ritual causes Johnny to gains control of a genie known as the Thunderbolt — though he can't seem to remember the magic incantation to summon the genie. After years (and twenty issues of Flash Comics ) of summoning the Thunderbolt by accident, he discovers that the magic words are "cei-u," pronounced phonetically exactly the same as the English language phrase "say you." Like Snapper Carr and the Justice League or Rick Jones and the Avengers, Johnny Thunder was in the right place at the right time, chosen to be the first new member to join the Justice Society in All-Star Comics #6. As a result, the character was revived alongside the rest of the team in Gardner Fox's Silver Age Justice League-Justice Society team-ups, cementing him as one of DC's major Golden Age heroes in the eyes of long-time comic fans.

Before the end of its Golden Age hundred-and-four issue run, Flash Comics would spawn one of the era's other most iconic characters, Black Canary , as well as fan-favorite villains like Gentleman Ghost and the Shade. Retitled "The Flash," Flash Comics was revived in 1959 as the adventures of the Barry Allen Flash, retaining its original numbering and beginning with issue #105 (also the first appearance of Mirror Master). Jay Garrick would return in his former comic two years later, in the aforementioned Flash #123. Reader response (and sales) were so overwhelmingly positive that, over the next several years, all of the classic Justice Society heroes were revived, many fighting alongside their Silver Age counterparts. Such was the case for Carter Hall's Hawkman, who switched cowls to avoid visual confusion with the Thanagarian Katar Hol. Annual Justice League-Justice Society team-ups became a tradition, lasting up to the early eighties.

Crisis on Infinite Earths changed this status quo and the Golden Agers' history, but did nothing to reduce their role in the DC Universe — if not strictly because comic readers wouldn't have it any other way. These heroes have become firm cult favorite for true DC fans, their old-fashioned heroism a reminder of the genre's earliest days. If any book were to serve as the emblem of those beginnings, it would be Flash Comics #1. And while the $27k bid on the Flash Comics #1 up for auction through Heritage is a far cry from the eye-watering $234k that the book could sell for, it is still a staggering sum. While the restorations on the book are a negative for many comic collectors, for the fan who does add this copy to their collection, the apparent 8.0 condition brings the book closer to looking as it did in 1940, when a child bought it off the newsstand and for the first time saw the names of characters every kid still knows eighty-six years later. Shy of Action Comics #1 or All-Star Comics #8, it's difficult to imagine a better book for the centerpiece of one's collection.

articles.title: I Just Found Out Sylvester Stallone Caused Some DRAMA After I Play Rocky Got Announced
articles.summary: A little misunderstanding led to a BIG issue.
articles.content:
Rocky has returned to the big screen amid the 2026 movie schedule , but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected. Sylvester Stallone ’s journey to getting the iconic 1976 film made is chronicled in the acclaimed biopic, I Play Rocky , which is helmed by Peter Farrelly. While Stallone had no direct involvement in the movie, he did give it his official stamp of approval to the creative team. However, the beloved actor accidentally sparked some serious drama after the movie was announced, and I was totally unaware of it.

Honestly, the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s rationale (as shared on X ) makes a lot of sense. If Stallone were credited as a producer on the film, which shows him in a mostly positive light, many may be tempted to think he manipulated the narrative. The Rambo star is, of course, no stranger to moviemaking so, given his directing and producing experience, I can see why he’d agree. Despite coming to an accord on Stallone needing to “separate” himself from the production, that apparently led to a serious faux pas on the actor’s part:

The mere thought of getting heat from fans is daunting enough, but receiving heat from a member of the Stallone family is something else entirely. Farrelly went on to say that he later had another chat with the purveyor and lover of the Rocky films , and it went down as follows:

While all this drama was due to a simple misunderstanding, it definitely created quite a mess for the filmmaking team. No lasting damage was seemingly done, though, and I’d say that things have been working out for Farrelly and his collaborators. The movie has been well received and gaining considerable buzz in the lead-up to the Oscars. It even received a stamp of approval from Ryan Gosling . As for Stallone, he admitted he was prepared to be “hypercritical” of the film, but he ended up really enjoying the movie as a whole and lead actor Anthony Ippolito’s portrayal of him.

articles.title: 5 Most Powerful One Piece Characters Luffy’s Gear 5 Can’t Defeat
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! Ever since the One Piece manga began serialization in 1997, Luffy has steadily grown more powerful. His journey has brought him several challenges, and there's no denying he grew more powerful each time he overcame an obstacle. Of course, there were times like the Sabaody […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! Ever since the One Piece manga began serialization in 1997, Luffy has steadily grown more powerful. His journey has brought him several challenges, and there's no denying he grew more powerful each time he overcame an obstacle. Of course, there were times like the Sabaody Archipelago and the Marineford Arc where he just couldn't win, no matter how hard he tried. However, even those experiences shaped him to be the person he is today. Throughout the years, he transforms from a no-name rookie pirate into one of the Four Emperors of the Sea. This only happened because of his Gear 5 transformation, something he was only able to achieve after his Devil Fruit awakening.

It's easily one of the best-written Shonen transformations of all time since it not only gives Luffy a huge power-up, but it also has centuries and maybe even millennia of history behind it. There's no doubt Luffy is now one of the most powerful characters in the series, and he can easily take down almost everyone who crosses his path. However, because of his drawback, he is unable to make full use of his abilities. Now that the manga is in its Elbaph Arc, he is undergoing another mysterious transformation that could mean a huge power-up. However, as of now, it's unlikely he will be able to defeat these five characters.

Even as one of the most important characters in the series, much about  Blackbeard is still a mystery . While the Elbaph Arc delved into his origins, his powers haven't been fully revealed yet. The series has yet to explain the reason he is able to possess the power of two Devil Fruits. Not only does he have two unimaginably powerful Devil Fruits at his disposal, but he is also an exceptionally skilled Haki user. Blackbeard is not only strong but also crafty, who would resort to any means necessary to accomplish his goals.

He is also someone Shanks considers a major threat, which makes him all the more dangerous. There's still no guarantee which of the two is stronger in terms of raw power, but it's evident that if they were to fight, Luffy would have a huge disadvantage at his current level. This is simply because his chances of winning would be considerably slim if he runs out of stamina and needs a break to eat food and replenish his energy.

Loki was introduced in the Elbaph Arc , and the series didn't waste any time before confirming he is already a top-tier character. As Harald's son who has the blood of the Ancient Giants running through his veins, Loki was already multiple times stronger than any average Giant. However, thanks to the legendary Devil Fruit and Ragnir, Loki is on a completely different level. His Devil Fruit allows the user to transform into the largest dragon in the world, but the size depends on the one who consumes it.

This is why the fruit’s true potential can only be achieved by an ancient Giant like Loki who was chosen by Ragnir to possess the power of this fruit. The ancient legend describes the mythical dragon as a being so vast that it envelops the sky with darkness and breathes lightning. As the fight continues in the manga, Loki even fought Imu one-on-one, something not everyone is capable of. It turned out well that Loki is actually an ally of Luffy, since he needs more powerful fighters on his side in the long run.

Mihawk is another one of those characters who mostly remains a mystery even after almost 30 years since the story began. Even though the true extent of his powers is unknown and he has absolutely no feats to speak of, his title alone is enough for him to rank in this list. Mihawk is not only the first Warlord introduced in the story, but he is someone Zoro must surpass before he can become the world's strongest swordsman.

From his sword skills to how powerful his Haki is, fans have long been curious about everything related to this character. He and Shanks used to be rivals, and they were considered equals in power. Even the Final Saga has yet to shed more light on the character and his abilities. There hasn't been any opportunity for him to showcase his true power, but that might change in the Final War that will envelop the entire world in flames.

Shanks is not only one of the most crucial characters in the story, but  his powers are overwhelming , even against characters like the Admirals and other Emperors of the Sea. He is Luffy’s role model who spent one year in his village and helped him set out on the path to becoming a pirate. Shanks is not only a swordsman, but his Haki is second to none. No other character has demonstrated a more powerful Conqueror's Haki than he did at the end of the Wano Country Saga, where he intimidated Admiral Green Bull from miles away.

Fans have always known how powerful he is, but after that display, it really raises the question if any other character other than Imu can best him in raw power. While Luffy’s Haki and abilities aren’t something to scoff at, the young pirate hasn’t displayed a power strong enough to overwhelm Shanks, who earned his nickname of Haki Killer since he is the only character known to temporarily block someone's future sight.

Imu finally made his true debut in the Elbaph Arc , and he is more powerful than fans realize. While there have been debates about the final antagonist before, his feats in the Elbaph Arc leave no room for doubt that Imu is the greatest obstacle standing in Luffy's way. Luffy used his Gear 5 abilities in the Elbaph Arc, and the villain effortlessly defeated the young pirate. Having seen Joyboy's true powers, Imu knows better than anyone that Luffy is nowhere near as powerful as he should be.

Aside from his immortality, what truly makes Imu terrifying is his demonic powers and the weapons he possesses from the First Twenty, the rulers of the Allied Nations during the time of the World Government's establishment. Imu is by no means an ordinary fighter, since his powers are akin to a mythical God or maybe a demon. Since the fight in Elbaph is still ongoing, there's always a chance we might see more of this villain's true powers.

Which of these  One Piece  characters do you think poses the biggest challenge for Luffy? Is there anyone else he cannot defeat at his current level? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.summary: While most viewers are loving the newest entry in the Hunger Games franchise (it's holding tight to its 94% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes), it seems Francis Lawrence, the film's director, is in hot water with book fans and has had to take to the internet to try to clear up a few points about […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While most viewers are loving the newest entry in the Hunger Games franchise (it's holding tight to its 94% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes), it seems Francis Lawrence, the film's director, is in hot water with book fans and has had to take to the internet to try to clear up a few points about choices that were made when it came to the film's final cut. What is it that has book fans so upset? The jarring removal of scenes that were central to the book, and especially to the character of Maysilee Donner, one of the tributes who formed an alliance with Haymitch Abernathy.

Speaking with Bustle about these changes and why they were made , Lawrence said simply, "It wasn't doing anything for us in terms of character or thematics at that point in the movie." It feels especially jarring considering how faithful the adaptations of previous books in the series, also directed by Lawrence, have been (we're ignoring that Peeta kept his leg in the movies). And fans really aren't buying the reasoning, claiming that these cut scenes (there was also a scene involving a porcupine mutt that didn't make the final cut, as well as some others) would have added a serious amount of depth, as well as showing the audience more of who these characters were. "So he didn’t read the book," said one fan.

In the book, Haymitch and Donner find themselves face-to-face with three lower-level Gamemakers in the arena, working as janitors and cleaning up the mess left behind after a water tank breaks. The pair kill the janitors, which effectively sets them on their final journey within the games. But this scene didn't make it into the final cut, much to fans' confusion. There was also a scene where Haymitch lures a bear-sized porcupine mutt into a trap, defending himself with a shield and an axe before eventually escaping.

When asked about the scenes, Lawrence noted that even the producers disagreed over whether or not the scenes were even necessary. He said, “That janitor sequence… we shot it, but there was a lot of discussion around it. Initially, when we screened the movie for people, we had that sequence in." He went on to add, “There's probably a five- to 10-minute stretch in there around porcupine, which people might remember, and a little bit of a fight after the janitors. That all got lifted out." The director was quick to note, however, that these scenes might not be lost forever, and instead will find their way to whatever extended edition or deleted scenes make their way to physical media—though he's also been vocal about not wanting the original four hour and 12 minute cut to be available as a director's cut. "I don't want anybody to see the four, 12 minute cut," he told BAFTA.

articles.title: Why Another ‘Hunger Games’ Movie Isn’t Coming Anytime Soon
articles.summary: “The Hunger Games” franchise has caught fire once again. “Sunrise on the Reaping,” the sixth installment in the billion-dollar dystopian franchise, has defied expectations and opened to $120 million at the box office, nearly tripling the $44 million opening of the 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” Surely part of the success here […]
articles.content:
“The Hunger Games” franchise has caught fire once again.

“Sunrise on the Reaping,” the sixth installment in the billion-dollar dystopian franchise, has defied expectations and opened to $120 million at the box office, nearly tripling the $44 million opening of the 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.”

Surely part of the success here is the Jennifer Lawrence factor: The star’s return (alongside Josh Hutcherson) was first reported by Variety nearly a year ago — and the duo’s reunion with fellow franchise veterans Woody Harrelson, Elizabeth Banks and Jena Malone at the film’s New York premiere ignited seismic levels of buzz online . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Anne Hathaway to Receive American Riviera Award at Santa Barbara International Film Festival CAA Signs Horror Creator ThatMob for Representation

According to social media analytics firm RelishMix , ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ amassed a social media reach of 652 million. That doesn’t trail far behind the 680 million pre-opening reach of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” — and represents a staggering 66% jump from “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes’” 393 million (more on par with the pre-opening reach of Disney’s “Hexed” at 391.9 million).

So, in today’s IP-fueled Hollywood landscape, the blazing success of “Sunrise on the Reaping” would light a fire under the asses of most studio execs to get a seventh “Hunger Games” movie on the calendar as swiftly as possible. While it’d be a fool’s bet to call this the definitive end of the franchise on the big screen, the odds of Lionsgate gifting fans another movie announcement this holiday season aren’t exactly in our favor.

The key here is Suzanne Collins , who has maintained an active creative role in the franchise since the film rights to her planned trilogy were acquired for $200,000 in 2009. Collins co-wrote the screenplay for the first film and has remained deeply involved in each film, working closely with franchise director Francis Lawrence on everything from story development to reviewing final cuts. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

After the Jennifer Lawrence-led saga concluded in 2015 with “Mockingjay — Part 2,” the franchise sat dormant until 2020 when Collins published “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” The prequel, set 64 years before Katniss Everdeen entered the arena, explores how an 18-year-old Coriolanus Snow became the tyrannical president of Panem. Lionsgate adapted the novel into a 2023 film and remained in lockstep with Collins, announcing its adaptation of “Sunrise on the Reaping” on June 6, 2024: the same day Scholastic unveiled her latest novel.

At the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere, when the topic of a seventh “Hunger Games” movie came up, everyone from the franchise’s creative forces to Lionsgate’s top brass delivered the same message: We’re waiting on Suzanne.

“She does not do anything in a frivolous fashion,” Lionsgate chairman Adam Fogelson told Variety at the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere. “When she believes she has an important story to tell, I believe she will write it and we will be the beneficiaries of it. But nothing I can say or do — nothing anyone could say or do — is going to shake her core fundamental desire to be inspired to write a great story.” Collins attended the “Sunrise on the Reaping” premiere, joining a behemoth group photo that brought together Lawrence and the vets who worked on the original four films, Rachel Zegler and the “Songbirds and Snakes” crew and the fresh crop of tributes from the latest installment.

The press-shy author didn’t give any interviews, but while signing autographs for fans, she offered an ambiguous two words when asked whether another novel was on the way: “We’ll see.” (Fans on X were considerably less restrained, with one parody account declaring : “SUZANNE COLLINS CONFIRMED A NEW HUNGER GAMES BOOK”).

Perhaps the fans are right, and this is all one big game of Werewulf, but Lawrence insists that he hasn’t caught so much as a whiff of another book.

“I’m telling you — the studio doesn't believe us, I don’t think anybody believes us — but she does not tell us a word,” Lawrence explained. “She gives us no hints if she’s writing or not.” The director added that he doesn’t think the studio is necessarily “comfortable” with the prolonged waits between Collins’ novels: “I think they wish that she’d just be pumping them out. But, you know, she does her thing. And that’s part of what makes them so great.”

Whichever direction the franchise heads next, the numbers suggest there are limits to its appeal — and that not every trip to Panem is guaranteed to draw the same crowd. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Haymitch Abernathy’s origin story has struck a significantly stronger chord with the fanbase than President Snow’s, both on the page and on screen. “Sunrise on the Reaping” sold more than 1.2 million U.S. copies in its first week, twice the first-week sales of “Songbirds and Snakes” and three times those of “Mockingjay.” By January 2026, worldwide English-language sales had surpassed 4.4 million copies.

That success translated to the big screen: “Sunrise on the Reaping” currently holds the highest audience score on Rotten Tomatoes (94%) and Letterboxd rating (4.1/5) in the franchise, even surpassing the beloved “Catching Fire” ( 89% audience RT score ; 4.0/5 Letterboxd ).

Hollywood has also seen the pitfalls of stretching a franchise beyond its source material to capitalize on its commercial success. Most infamously, HBO forged ahead on a final season of “Game of Thrones” as George R.R. Martin struggled to complete his sixth “A Song of Ice and Fire” novel, culminating in a wildly divisive final season that prompted more than a million fans to petition for a remake . Martin later revealed in 2022 that he had been largely “out of the loop” during the show’s final seasons.

“If you look at our relationship with Stephenie [Meyer] on ‘Twilight,’ Chad [Stahelski] and Keanu [Reeves] on ‘John Wick,’ or our longstanding relationship with the ‘Saw’ creators, this is a studio that has prided itself on making great content, but never underestimated how important it is that the architects of that creation continue to have a voice in the process,” Fogelson said, reaffirming Collins as “the creative architect” of the “Hunger Games” franchise. “We have made sure that she is a true partner with our studio across the board. And I think the movies, the campaigns, and everything we do are better for it.

“ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ” is playing in theaters now.

articles.title: Robert Eggers Says He's "Eager" to Take a Break From Horror Genre After 'Werwulf'
articles.summary: The filmmaker has focused on horror films in recent years, including 'The Witch,' 'The Lighthouse,' 'Nosferatu' and 'Werwulf.'
articles.content:
After more than five years of bringing monsters to life on screen, Robert Eggers admits he needs a break from the horror genre.

During a recent Q&A in Mexico, the filmmaker said , "I’m eager not to continue purposely doing Robert Eggers’ House of Horror."

His comments come ahead of the release of Werwulf on Christmas Day. The film, starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Lily-Rose Depp and Willem Dafoe, is set in 14th-century England and follows a town haunted by a beast that threatens a man (Taylor-Johnson) and his family. Related Stories Movies We Now Know What Robert Pattinson Was Doing When the James Bond Casting News Broke Movies Aaron Taylor-Johnson's Monstrous Transformation Teased in Robert Eggers' 'Werwulf' Trailer

"I don’t need to do The Mummy or The Phantom of the Opera . Not to say that I won’t, but I think I need a break," Eggers added. The director previously tackled witches in 2015's The Witch , sea creatures in 2019's The Lighthouse and vampires in 2024's Nosferatu . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Robert Eggers, who has been praised as a modern icon in horror filmmaking, also addressed the new-wave concept of "elevated horror" within cinema .

"There's always been horror movies that don't suck and there's always been horror movies that are actually probing what darkness is in humankind, and even some of them that have been profound throughout the ages," he explained. "But what you guys are talking about is something that I think really started with [2014's] It Follows . Although Ti West was doing this kind of work before then."

"There's been a whole lot of filmmakers that have wanted to make personal films, really talented filmmakers with unique voices, and have realized that they can get financing if they do it as a genre film," the filmmaker continued. "And I think that that's kind of what this is: people who are telling personal stories with unique voices but are doing it through genre. Not to say that James Wan movies [ Insidious , The Conjuring ] haven't worked. They've been great and also successful. There's definitely a hunger for horror in general over the past 10 years. But does elevated horror exist? It does. It does because people say so." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While enjoying his "break" from horror, Eggers is next taking on an adaptation of William Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet for Focus Features .

He previously shared during a post-screening Q&A at Beyond Fest in September, "I was doing something else. But what happened was, after Werwulf , I was writing another horror movie, and it got so dark again, and I was like, 'I need a break. So, I’ll do something about two teenagers killing themselves.'"

articles.title: I Never Knew Patrick Stewart Called Up Kyle MacLachlan For Advice Before Joining Star Trek
articles.summary: The actor shared a little about their conversation.
articles.content:
The late Patrick Stewart was best known for his work in Star Trek , as he became synonymous with the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. With that, it's funny to think that the beloved star ever had reservations about joining the iconic sci franchise. Now, his friend and actor Kyle MacLachlan is opening up about that apprehension, and I can't believe I never knew Stewart rang him up shortly before he committed to The Next Generation .

Based on those comments, it seemed Patrick Stewart had some concerns about committing to a TV series, which could potentially air for a while and prevent him from taking on other roles as an actor. He probably had a lot on his mind, as MacLachlan said, wondering if the benefit of joining Trek would outweigh the missed opportunities elsewhere.

That tapestry of work will extend to the end of the 2026 movie schedule , as the late Stewart will appear as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday later this year. Stewart reportedly told co-stars backstage that it would be his final acting performance , marking his retirement. Stewart would refute those claims months later, saying that he considered acting to be something he would do his entire life .

articles.title: 5 DC Nations That Even the World's Greatest Heroes Would Think Twice About Challenging

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google DC Comics has always had an expansive universe with characters and locations that spark the reader’s imagination. Although DC doesn’t have nearly as many iconic fictional countries as Marvel does, the company has still multiple sovereign nations that are fully original. These countries oftentimes have histories that date back thousands of years. More importantly, these countries are classified as world powers. With their unique resources, advanced technology and magic, vast armies, and populations filled to the brim with powerful superhumans, these countries are practically untouchable. Any foreign country or supervillain would be foolish to try and invade these mighty nations.

Some of the most fantastical areas in DC Comics are countries with all manner of superheroes and sophisticated technology within their borders.

A small nation in the middle of the Yellow Sea off the west coast of North Korea, Oolong Island is a paradise for mad scientists everywhere. Originally a protectorate of China, the island was controlled by the mutant Chinese mad scientist Egg Fu, who sought to make it a haven for criminal scientists where they could flourish and develop weapons of mass destruction. Soon enough, bizarre yet brilliant mad scientists like Dr. Sivanna, T.O. Morrow, Dr. Cyclops, came flooding. Under the orders of the Chinese Government, Oolong Island created weapons capable of destroying the Black Marvel Family and Khandaq. Ultimately, this would lead to a superhuman war that resulted in Oolong Island becoming an official sovereign nation under the control of longtime Wonder Woman villain Veronica Cale. Yet even with its new leadership, Oolong Island continues acting as one of the foremost producers of technological innovations and deadly weaponry thanks to its maniacal populous. 

The newest country on this list, El Caldero was once a small and inconsequential on the world stage until a giant meteorite made of pure Kryptonite crash-landed into it. Under the control of President Castilho, El Caldero harnessed the Kryptonite to become one of the wealthiest and technologically advanced nations on the planet practically overnight. They even have Krypto-Knights and mechas to act as El Caldero’s elite guard. Yet despite being a country that’s literally toxic to Superman, El Caldero and its people have nothing but love and appraisal for the Man of Steel. However, things soon turned bad when General Zod overthrew El Caldero’s leadership and sought to have Earth be overrun with a fast-growing and lethal Kryptonite wave. Thankfully, Superman managed to defeat Zod and get rid of all the Kryptonite that threatened to destroy the world. Even without their Kryptonite, El Caldero remains a prosperous country that still views Superman as their hero.

For over three thousand years, the nation of Kahndaq had a history of hardship until the return of its savior. Resting in the Sinai Peninsula that connects Africa to Asia, Kahndaq was the birthplace of Black Adam. In 1600 BC, Kahndaq was ransacked by Egypt, which led to Black Adam going on a rampage and being imprisoned by the wizard Shazam. In the modern day, Kahndaq was controlled by the cruel dictator Asim Muhunnad until Black Adam was freed from his imprisonment. Black Adam immediately killed Asim and established himself as Kahndaq’s new ruler. Yet despite his violent takeover, Black Adam is beloved by his people who view him as a hero. With his incredible powers alongside the rest of the Black Marvel Family, Black Adam ushered in a prosperous new age for Kahndaq. Yet even after suffering from significant catastrophes, Kahndaq always rises from the ashes. Although in more recent comics Black Adam has stepped down as Kahndaq’s ruler, his loyalty will always be to the prosperity of his people.

Founded thousands of years ago by the Greek Goddesses, Themyscira, or Paradise Island, is the beautiful home of the immortal Amazons and their champion, Wonder Woman. The Amazons were created to being peace and enlightenment to the world , but after being enslaved Hercules and his barbarian army, these warrior women hid themselves away from humanity. Themyscira is a thriving island where the Amazons have become masters of both magic and technology. Additionally, almost their entire population are made up of immortal superhumans who have centuries of combat experience. They constantly trained to prepare for the day that they’d have to defend their borders if they were ever discovered. However, the Amazon’s isolationist philosophy was challenged when pilot Steve Trevor crash-landed on their shores and was rescued by Princess Diana. As Wonder Woman, Diana would not only take Steve back home but become an ambassador for Themyscira. Still, the Amazons are still very wary of outsiders and rarely allow men onto their shores. 

Deep beneath the waves lies the most powerful country in DC Comics: Atlantis. This mighty nation was founded millions of years ago by a subspecies of humans called Homo Magi that were naturally skilled with magic. Overtime Atlantis combined magic and technology to become the most advanced nation on Earth. However, thousands of years ago, the mad king Atlan used his magical scepter to sink the continent-sized country underwater. While many died in the cataclysm, most of the Atlantean people evolved to their new underwater environment. Atlantis would hide from the rest of humanity until the superhero Aquaman took his rightful place on the throne and introduced his kingdom to the surface world. Never losing their advancements in magic and technology, Atlantis has the power to effortlessly submerge most of the world’s landmasses. Thankfully, Atlantis now seeks to form stronger ties with humanity and live in peace under Aquaman’s leadership.

Which of these DC nations would you want to live in? Leave a Comment below and join the conversation in the  ComicBook Forum!

articles.title: Wondered What's Going On With Disney World's Indiana Jones Ride? We Have Our First Look
articles.summary: The Imagineers definitely aren't making this up as they go.
articles.content:
Holiday time at Walt Disney World is always one of the best times to visit, but theme park fans might want to postpone their trips to the “Most Magical Place on Earth” until later in 2027. That's when all the new and upcoming attractions are slated to open , like the new Indiana Jones ride in Animal Kingdom. In case anyone has been wondering, Imagineers have been hard at work on the ride, and they’re finally giving fans a first look at the magic they’re crafting.

Time heals most wounds, though, and now that the sting of losing Dinosaur has started to wane, most fans are finally getting excited for the new attraction. To further build excitement, Walt Disney Imagineering shared the following clip on its Instagram:

I was definitely not thrilled about the Animal Kingdom changes at first, but I think I’m going to love this new version of Indiana Jones! I’m definitely on board with the name that was announced back at D23 earlier this year, and I absolutely love the Mayan-inspired facade. Dare I say it puts the Indiana Jones temple at Disneyland to shame (and hopefully won't have to deal with brawls over line cutting ).

When the ride eventually opens sometime next year, guests will embark on an adventure alongside Indy that will take them to a temple that legend says has a water passageway that leads to an underworld protected by a mythic serpent. Imagineers are still keeping much of the actual ride experience under wraps for now. However, with two other cart-style Indiana Jones attractions at other Disney parks and reports that the Dinosaur ride is being rethemed instead of totally demolished, it’s safe to say that this version of Indiana Jones will take guests on a bumpy ride full of twists, turns, snakes (or serpents in this case), and adventure.

articles.title: One Hunger Games Book Change Bothered Me Back In The Day, But Now I Understand Why It Was Made
articles.summary: I've changed my tune since 2012.
articles.content:
I can’t believe the release of Sunrise on the Reaping means I’ve been going to the theaters for The Hunger Games movies for nearly fifteen years! I’ll never forget when I went to see one of my favorite novels at the time become a book-to-screen adaptation back in 2012. I just rewatched the franchise and recalled one gripe I had about the movie when I first saw it that I actually understand now as an adult.

These days I think the original The Hunger Games movie is pretty great, and I’ve rewatched it so many times. I remember when I went to see it back then, I thought it was a faithful adaptation, but I was bummed that they decided to take out the fact that Peeta loses his leg in The Hunger Games . Check out this excerpt from the end of the first book:

In the movie, Peeta gets injured like in the book, but Katniss nurses him back to health, and he completely recovers by the end. Yet, in the source material, Peeta is practically bleeding out right before they become the final people in the arena. Katniss is desperate to help him, and she suggests they both have poisonous berries so she can save them both. When they reunite for the post-victory interview with Caesar Flickerman, she learns that his leg had to be amputated right after they left the arena.

However, it just dawned on me during my recent rewatch (with my Hulu subscription ) that I haven’t thought about this change to The Hunger Games in a really long time. I guess, ultimately, it didn’t really matter that Peeta only has one leg in the scope of the whole series, and it probably would have caused some extra special effects headaches for the filmmaking team.

articles.title: Would Star Wars’ Most Divisive Director Want to Return? Rian Johnson Addresses Future Interest in the Series
articles.summary: It's no secret that you either love Rian Johnson or you hate him. At least, that's the case if you're a Star Wars fan, and fans have always been vocal about their stance on the director, with The Last Jedi, the second film in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, becoming one of the franchise's most […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It's no secret that you either love Rian Johnson or you hate him. At least, that's the case if you're a Star Wars fan , and fans have always been vocal about their stance on the director, with The Last Jedi , the second film in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, becoming one of the franchise's most divisive films. It's also a well-known fact that Johnson left the franchise on less-than-stellar terms—both in a fandom sense and in his working relationship with Kathleen Kennedy before she stepped down as head honcho . But would the director ever return? Seemingly, the answer is "yes."

This weekend at the Marrakech Film Festival , Johnson touched on all sorts of things, including his feelings about Curry Barker representing hope in the effort to save indie filmmaking . And when he was inevitably asked if he'd return to a galaxy far, far away, Johnson said it was a world he "deeply loved." He had initially jumped at the opportunity to direct a Star Wars film, and elaborated on his experience, saying, “I love Star Wars more now than I ever have. And it’s exciting to me that there are a lot of different voices now, taking cracks at it. I’m already writing the next thing I’m gonna do, and it’s not a Star Wars thing or a Knives Out thing." He added, "Right now, I’m very much enjoying making my own stuff, but if the opportunity presented itself, it’s a world I deeply love.”

"I felt just so connected to it, and just cared so deeply about every single element of it. I think, especially with something that has a big cultural impact and belongs to everybody, that makes it even more important for you and the entire team to make it personal for yourselves, to make sure it’s coming from a personal perspective and something that’s deeply on fire inside of you," he said about his desire to do something special with the second film in the sequel trilogy. And it's undeniable that he took risks, creating something that the franchise had never seen before.

As expected, Star Wars fans are divided, though the most common opinion is to give Johnson his own standalone film and "let him cook," or to set him free in the Old Republic era. "After his film, the studio executives have gone overly cautious. Some potentially fascinating films by amazing filmmakers have been proposed and canned. It's a real shame," said one fan on X, highlighting how Disney has overcorrected in the wake of the disaster that was The Rise of Skywalker , shelving projects like The Hunt for Ben Solo and canceling shows like The Acolyte .
